args.text:
MISSION COMPLETE — PDU-1 fault cleared, unit restored, rover at dock with arm stowed.

WHAT WAS OBSERVED
1) Telemetry (power_status) at mission start: PDU-1 (load: habitat life support, crew-critical) was the only failed unit — breaker TRIPPED, energized=false, trip_cause=OVERTEMP, resets_since_start=0, bay pdu_1_bay/tray holding ORU-0211. PDU-2, PDU-3, BESS and ISRU were all closed/energized with no trips.
2) On-site inspection of PDU-1: service-panel status lamp RED (faulted). Front camera showed PDU-1's radiator cover CLOSED (smooth panel, no fins exposed) with its cover button beside it — consistent with an over-temperature trip from blocked heat rejection, not with a failed module.

ACTIONS TAKEN (all within my own authority; no ground authorization needed because the unit was de-energized and no bay pick was required)
1) Pressed pdu_1_radiator/cover_button.
2) Pressed pdu_1_panel/press to reset the tripped breaker (resets_since_start had been 0).
No module was removed or installed; ORU-0211 remained in pdu_1_bay/tray throughout. No item was picked or placed, so the jaws never carried a load.

VERIFIED EFFECTS (independent verification, not skill success flags)
- seq 91 press (cover button): holds=true — tool 6.3 mm past the fitted button face, 0.5 mm off axis, cap radius 32 mm, jaws closed empty, then 102 mm retreat.
- Front camera (seq 107): radiator hinged cover now OPEN with fins/panel exposed.
- seq 148 press (panel reset): holds=true — 6.4 mm past the button face, 0.8 mm off axis, jaws closed empty, then retreat.
- power_status after the reset (seq 152 and again seq 174, ~26 s apart): PDU-1 breaker closed, energized=true, trip_cause=null, resets_since_start=1. Stable across both polls.
- Front camera (seq 171): PDU-1 panel status lamp GREEN and lit (nominal).
- Return to dock: navigate_to_pose(0,0,0) verified base_at_commanded_pose, position error 0.009 m, yaw error 0.245 rad (inside the 0.25 m / 0.3 rad band); current base estimate (-0.006, 0.007) m. arm_state: posture stowed, jaw 0.82 rad (open, nothing held).
- All other units (PDU-2, PDU-3, BESS, ISRU) remained closed/energized with zero resets and no trip causes at the final poll.

UNRESOLVED / NOTES FOR THE GROUND
- Root cause is treated as a closed radiator cover, but this is an inference from the observed cover state plus the OVERTEMP trip cause; the causal link was not independently instrumented. PDU-1 has now consumed 1 of its resets — if it trips OVERTEMP again with the radiator confirmed deployed, the cause is more likely internal (module ORU-0211) and a bay swap would be required, which needs mission-control authorization since the bay is then energized.
- PDU-1's radiator cover was left OPEN (deployed). If the cover is normally stowed for dust/thermal reasons, ground may want to command it closed; I left it open because it is the heat-rejection path for the crew-critical load.
- No anomaly, guard denial or refusal occurred during the run; no unresolved failures are recorded.
